input.quote: 18.9 Assignment. This Agreement may not be assigned by either Party to any Third Party without the written consent of the other Party hereto; except either Party may assign this Agreement without the other Party's consent to an entity that acquires substantially all of the business or assets of the assigning Party, whether by merger, acquisition or otherwise; provided that the acquiring party agrees in a writing delivered to the non-assigning Party to assume all of the rights and obligations of the assigning Party under this Agreement.
input.rationale: Section 18.9 is symmetric and gives us a full M&A/successor carve-out: either Party (including Ono) may assign without the other's consent to an entity acquiring substantially all of its business or assets by merger, acquisition or otherwise, subject only to the acquirer's written assumption of obligations. Affiliate assignment is permitted under Section 18.9's second paragraph with the other Party's consent "not to be unreasonably withheld or delayed", which sits at the playbook fallback rather than the preferred consent-free affiliate right; the same is true of the unqualified consent standard for other Third Party assignments and the tax-consequences proviso, but these are mutual and are minor sub-elements only. On change of control, Section 18.10 imposes only firewall obligations following a Change in Control of Array (i.e., it binds the counterparty), and no provision gives Array any right to terminate, re-price or renegotiate on a Change in Control of Ono (Section 4.5(b) likewise terminates only on Array's Change in Control). Accordingly the clause meets the fallback on all material terms and no redline is warranted.
